item.title: Elder Bhadda: I was an only child, loved by father and mother. Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties. Out of compassion…
item.description:
Elder Bhadda:

I was an only child, loved by father and mother.
Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties.

Out of compassion for me, wishing for my happiness,
Both my father and mother led me to the Buddha.

'This son of ours, obtained with great difficulty,
Raised with delicacy, nurtured and cared for,
We respectfully offer him to you, O savior,
To serve as your attendant, to serve the conqueror.'

The Teacher accepted me, saying to Ānanda:
'Let him go forth; he will become virtuous.'

After the Teacher had me go forth,
The conqueror then entered the monastery.
Before the sun rose, my mind was liberated.

Then my Teacher, to complete the task,
From silent meditation, stood up and called me:
'Come, Bhadda.' Thus I received full ordination.

From birth, at seven years, I received full ordination.
I have attained the three knowledges — O Dhamma, good Dhamma-nature!

From: Theragāthā 7.3

item.title: Just as rust is born from iron, And, born, eats away the iron, So excessive gain and honor lead One's own deeds to a bad…
item.description:
Just as rust is born from iron,
And, born, eats away the iron,
So excessive gain and honor lead
One's own deeds to a bad destination.

Among these defilements,
Ignorance is the worst.
Bhikkhu, abandon that defilement,
Become free from defilements.

Easy is life for the shameless,
One who is bold as a crow,
One who is backbiting and boastful,
One who is reckless and defiled.

Difficult is life for the modest,
One who always seeks purity,
One who is unassuming and humble,
One who is pure and bright.

From: Dhammapada 235-255

item.title: There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful…
item.description:
There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful verbal formations, accumulates harmful mental formations. Having accumulated harmful bodily formations, harmful verbal formations, harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a harmful world. Being reborn in a harmful world, harmful contacts touch him. Touched by harmful contacts, he experiences harmful feelings, exclusively painful, like beings in hell. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a non-harmful world. Being reborn in a non-harmful world, non-harmful contacts touch him. Touched by non-harmful contacts, he experiences non-harmful feelings, exclusively pleasant, like the Subhakiṇha devas. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful. Being reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful, contacts that are both harmful and non-harmful touch him. Touched by them, he experiences feelings that are both harmful and non-harmful, a mixture of pleasure and pain, like humans, some devas, and some beings in the lower realms. These three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appear in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.23

item.title: Hard to find in the world is a person Who feels shame, who restrains himself, Who avoids reproach, Like a good horse avoids the whip.…
item.description:
Hard to find in the world is a person
Who feels shame, who restrains himself,
Who avoids reproach,
Like a good horse avoids the whip.

Like a good horse touched by the whip,
Be ardent and energetic.
With faith, virtue, and energy,
Concentration and investigation of states,
Endowed with clear knowledge and conduct, mindful,
Abandon this boundless suffering.

Irrigators guide water,
Fletchers shape arrows,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.

From: Dhammapada 129-145

item.title: Standing to one side, the devata Siva spoke this verse before the Blessed One: Associate with the good, Be close to the virtuous, Knowing the…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the devata Siva spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One only becomes better, not worse.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One gains wisdom, not otherwise.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One does not sorrow amidst sorrow.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
One shines among relatives.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
Beings are reborn in good destinations.
Associate with the good,
Be close to the virtuous,
Knowing the good Dhamma from the wise,
Beings always enjoy happiness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.21

item.title: Elder Talapuṭa (continued): Develop jhāna, faculties, powers, Develop concentration, factors of enlightenment, Realize the three knowledges in the Buddha's teaching. O mind, encourage me, advise…
item.description:
Elder Talapuṭa (continued):

Develop jhāna, faculties, powers,
Develop concentration, factors of enlightenment,
Realize the three knowledges in the Buddha's teaching.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Develop the path to attain the Deathless,
The path leading to the penetration
Where all suffering is destroyed.
The eightfold path washing away all defilements —
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Contemplate the aggregates as suffering,
Abandon from you the causes of suffering.
In this very life, make an end of suffering.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Contemplate with wisdom: impermanent, suffering,
Empty, not-self, evil, murderous,
Restrain your mind, do not let it run.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Shaven-headed and ugly, going about reviled,
When begging alms from families, holding a skull-shaped bowl —
Now are you focused on the Teacher's instruction,
The word of the great seer? O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Walk on the path with self well tamed,
Among houses, with mind not attached to sensual desires,
Like the full moon without a cloud.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

Live in the forest, eat almsfood,
Dwell in a charnel ground, wear dust-heap robes,
Always sitting, never lying down,
Delight in the ascetic practices.
O mind, encourage me, advise me as before.

From: Theragāthā 19.1

item.title: And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, what is dwelling in heedfulness? One who lives restraining the eye faculty, bhikkhus, his mind is not stained by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. ... the ear faculty ... the nose faculty ... the tongue faculty ... the body faculty ... One who lives restraining the mind faculty, his mind is not stained by mind-objects cognizable by the mind. For one with an unstained mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences happiness. For one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. With concentration, phenomena become manifest. When phenomena are manifest, that person is called one who dwells in heedfulness. Thus, bhikkhus, is dwelling in heedfulness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.97

item.title: Poṭṭhapāda, when defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive…
item.description:
Poṭṭhapāda, when defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive wisdom, then joy arises, gladness, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, in the autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun rises in the sky, dispelling all darkness from space, shining,…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, in the autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun rises in the sky, dispelling all darkness from space, shining, glowing, and radiating. So too, bhikkhus, by developing and cultivating the perception of impermanence, all sensual lust is abandoned, all lust for form is abandoned, all craving for existence is abandoned, all ignorance is abandoned, all conceit is uprooted. How is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated, bhikkhus, so that all sensual lust is abandoned ... all conceit is uprooted? This is form; this is the arising of form; this is the cessation of form. This is feeling ... this is perception ... these are formations ... this is consciousness; this is the arising of consciousness; this is the cessation of consciousness. The perception of impermanence developed and cultivated in this way, bhikkhus, leads to the abandoning of all sensual lust, all lust for form, all craving for existence, all ignorance, and the uprooting of all conceit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.102

item.title: Because of robes, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of almsfood, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of lodgings, bhikkhus, craving arises for…
item.description:
Because of robes, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of almsfood, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of lodgings, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. Because of this or that kind of existence, bhikkhus, craving arises for a bhikkhu. These are the four kinds of arising of craving from which craving arises for a bhikkhu.

One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time.
He does not transcend the round of existence,
From this life to the next.

Knowing this danger,
That craving gives birth to suffering,
Free from craving, without clinging,
Mindful, the bhikkhu wanders.

From: Itivuttaka 105
